builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features
summary: FeatureArc replaces single-request, fixed-codebase evaluations of coding agents with multi-stage tasks built from repository histories, where each stage extends the agent's own prior code and is checked with fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests. It costs benchmark construction and manual review effort (73 tasks of 2 to 10 stages, four languages), plus persistent-session agent runs without external test feedback; it requires no model training and runs within a single-GPU or API budget. It can fail as a selection tool if a team's real workloads are single-shot requests, if the pipeline mislabels F2P/P2P tests on non-reference code, or if small task counts make agent comparisons statistically unstable.
rationale: The reader adopting coding agents in production needs evaluation that reflects sequential, self-dependent work, and this benchmark's staged protocol is directly reusable at small scale without infrastructure beyond API access.
technique: Multi-stage evolving-feature benchmark for coding agents

claims.statement: FeatureArc replaces single-request, fixed-codebase evaluations of coding agents with multi-stage tasks built from repository histories, where each stage extends the agent's own prior code and is checked with fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests. It costs benchmark construction and manual review effort (73 tasks of 2 to 10 stages, four languages), plus persistent-session agent runs without external test feedback; it requires no model training and runs within a single-GPU or API budget. It can fail as a selection tool if a team's real workloads are single-shot requests, if the pipeline mislabels F2P/P2P tests on non-reference code, or if small task counts make agent comparisons statistically unstable.

No improvement claim; the paper reports a diagnostic finding: pooled agent success drops from 62.7% on first-stage tasks to 28.5% on whole features, with inherited defects present in 72.9% of failed later stages and left unnoticed roughly 95% of the time.
